description: Mid-size institutional research group building a centralized knowledge/search portal for analyst content, filings, and proprietary models. Priority: secure private deployment with dedicated inference capacity, strict residency + KMS integration for client data.
notes: Summary: RAG-first roadmap. Primary driver: faster, more accurate research search for analysts + compliance audit trail.
Scale: expected initial index 12–18M docs (PDFs, research notes, models), ~600GB vector store, growth to ~30M within 18 months.
Traffic profile: 8k–15k queries/day typical, peak 60k QPS spread across analysts at close windows. Target 95th latency for user-visible queries <250ms end-to-end (retrieve + rerank).
Cost targets (customer): avg $/query <= $0.10; preference to optimize per-query with batching, KV caching and specialized quantized models.
Security: must integrate with customer KMS (Azure Key Vault), attest SOC2 + iso27001 on vendor side, and provide audit logs for search queries and PII access.
Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity in customer VPC with private control plane; on-prem option for specific regulated desks.
Model preferences: open Llama-family variants for reranker (fine-tune allowed), embeddings via high-dim (1536–2048) with single-vector per doc + metadata keys for quick filtering.
Retrieval stack: currently PoC comparing Elastic ANN vs FAISS on-prem. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization + kernel selection to reduce GPU footprint.
POC notes: ingest milestone 1 (2M docs) completed 2024-10-21. Retrieval-only baseline: median 85ms for ANN top-100 on dedicated test cluster; reranker baseline (cpu) ~420ms — unacceptable.
Redwood POC: ran dedicated GPU reranker (small LM) — p50 170ms, p95 260ms when colocated with ANN service; positive feedback from data science team on quality uplift.
Security review status: initial questionnaire returned 2024-11-05. Legal flagged data residency clause (EU desk) and KMS provable zero-access requirement.
Quote from Head of Research (call 2024-11-12): 'We need a solution that *behaves* like an internal search — fast, auditable, and compliant.'
Commercial: procurement prefers annual committed reserved capacity. Customer looking for committed latency SLOs for analyst-facing routes; willing to trade cost for consistency.
Open technical asks: 1) RDF for incremental indexing and delta-updates for 100s of daily reports, 2) cold-start strategy for embargoed docs, 3) multi-region data residency partitioning.
Next technical workshop on 2024-12-03: Redwood infra + SE + Fenmore infra + legal to walk KMS integration, SSO mapping and dataflow diagrams.
Action items: SE to produce dedicated capacity sizing calc (requested 2024-11-20) — output needed to finalize SOW; PO to provide example retention policy for audit logs.
Internal notes (AE): keep messaging on cost controls (Optimize) and graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model) — resonates with procurement.
Sales play: propose 6-month pilot with committed GPU pool + opt-in auto-burst to hosted for peak windows; include one security workshop and SOC2 artifacts in SOW.
Risks: if Redwood cannot show KMS HSM sign-off and residency design, legal will push to on-prem procurement route (longer sales cycle).
